correctness.rationale: The proof is reconstructed from the definition. Centering and the \(t\) versus \(t+\pi\) parallelogram identity reduce the norm to a degree-two real-part envelope. Fejér--Riesz factorization gives \(p=xz\) and \(q\le y(x+z)\), reducing the envelope to minimizing \(u-2p+q^2/u\) over \(u\ge4p\). The two resulting branches are then combined with exact AM--GM bounds on \(AD\) and \(BC\). The final one-variable profiles have exact maxima \(\varphi^2\) and \(7/3\), respectively. The explicit polynomial has supremum \(5-\sqrt{5}\) by a concave quadratic in \(\sin^2 t\), giving ratio \(\varphi\). No finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The Sidon constant is a standard natural invariant, and \(\{-2,-1,1,2\}\) is the smallest symmetric nonzero four-frequency spectrum. The result is a sharp global constant for arbitrary complex coefficients, not a phase-only or equal-modulus slice. It supplies an exact four-element benchmark in a setting where the checked classical theory is complete only for three frequencies and special larger supports; the Fejér--Riesz envelope also isolates a reusable structural mechanism.
